info.description:
Programmatic, read-only access to Turing Station posts — the same content the website serves, over a small JSON API. Requests without credentials see publicly visible content; an API key unlocks whatever your membership includes.

# Getting started

1. Sign in on the Turing Station website and open **Settings → API keys**.
2. Create a key with a name that describes what will use it (e.g. "research agent"). The key is shown **once**, at creation — store it somewhere safe. You can keep up to 15 active keys and revoke any of them later.
3. Make your first request:

```bash
curl "https://api.turingstation.nl/content/posts?limit=5" \
  -H "X-API-Key: <your key>"
```


# Command line

[`tstation`](https://github.com/Bitcoin-Alpha/tstation) is the official CLI for this API. Try it without installing:

```bash
npx @label21/tstation posts list
```

Or install it globally to get the `tstation` command:

```bash
npm install -g @label21/tstation
```

Commands:

- `tstation posts list` — browse the feed, with `--tags`, `--search`, and `--featured` filters
- `tstation posts get <id-or-slug>` — read a post in your terminal
- `tstation posts tags` — list tags
- `tstation auth login` / `auth status` / `auth logout` — store, inspect, or remove your API key

Add `--json` to any command for raw output that pipes into `jq`. In scripts and CI, the `TSTATION_API_KEY` and `TSTATION_API_URL` environment variables override the stored configuration.

# MCP

AI assistants can use this API through the Model Context Protocol endpoint at `https://api.turingstation.nl/content/mcp`. It exposes five tools mirroring the REST surface:

- `list_posts` — compact post summaries, paginated, with tag, search, and featured filters
- `get_post` — a single post as plain text, by id or slug
- `list_tags` — all tags with post counts
- `list_transcripts` — podcast episode transcript summaries, with full-text search and ranked, highlighted snippets (requires an API key)
- `get_transcript` — one episode's transcript in paged windows (`offset`/`max_words`, follow `next_offset`), by show and episode number (requires an API key)

Authentication works exactly as for REST: the `X-API-Key` header is optional, anonymous access sees public content, and your key unlocks your membership's tiers. The transport is stateless Streamable HTTP, so any MCP client that can send a custom header works — no session management required. For Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http turingstation https://api.turingstation.nl/content/mcp --header "X-API-Key: <your key>"
```

In Claude Desktop, add a custom connector with the same URL and header.

get.description: Get all available post tags for filtering.

Get a single post. The formats query param selects the content representation: plaintext (default) and/or lexical, comma-separated. The path parameter accepts either a post UUID or a slug (SEO-friendly URLs). Access control is applied based on the user's subscription tier. When authenticated, includes reading_progress and is_bookmarked fields.
